q: What was Sputnik 1?
What was the first artificial satellite launched into space?
Which spacecraft marked the beginning of the Space Race?
a: Sputnik 1 was the first artificial Earth satellite, launched by the Soviet Union on October 4, 1957. It was a small metal sphere with four external radio antennas that emitted a steady beep, proving that orbital flight was possible.

q: Which cosmonaut became the first person to orbit the Earth?
Who was the first human to enter outer space?
a: Yuri Gagarin, a Soviet cosmonaut, became the first human in space on April 12, 1961. He flew the Vostok 1 spacecraft, completing a single orbit around the Earth in approximately 108 minutes.

q: What was the purpose of Project Mercury?
What were the goals of the United States' Project Mercury?
a: Project Mercury was the first human spaceflight program of the United States, designed to put a man into orbit around Earth. Its primary goals were to test a man's ability to function in space and to recover both the astronaut and the spacecraft safely.

q: What was the significance of the Apollo 11 mission?
Who were the first humans to walk on the moon?
What achievement defined the end of the Space Race?
a: Apollo 11 was the first crewed mission to land on the Moon, achieving this feat on July 20, 1969. Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin became the first humans to walk on the lunar surface, effectively winning the race to the Moon for the United States.

q: What was the Vostok program?
Which Soviet program launched the first humans into space?
What were the characteristics of the Vostok spacecraft?
a: The Vostok program was the first human spaceflight program conducted by the Soviet Union between 1960 and 1963. It utilized a spherical descent capsule and was designed to carry a single cosmonaut into low Earth orbit.

q: What was the role of Laika the dog in the Space Race?
Which animal was the first to orbit the Earth?
Why did the Soviets send Laika into space?
a: Laika was a stray dog from Moscow who became the first living creature to orbit the Earth aboard Sputnik 2 in 1957. Her mission was intended to prove that a living organism could survive the launch into orbit and the conditions of weightlessness.

q: What was the Gemini program?
How did Project Gemini bridge the gap between Mercury and Apollo?
What were the primary objectives of the Gemini missions?
a: The Gemini program was a NASA project conducted in the mid-1960s to develop techniques for long-duration flight and orbital rendezvous. It focused on mastering docking procedures and extravehicular activity (spacewalks), which were essential for the moon missions.

q: What was the Luna program?
Which Soviet missions first reached the surface of the Moon?
What were the goals of the Luna probes?
a: The Luna program was a series of robotic spacecraft sent by the Soviet Union to explore the Moon from 1959 to 1976. Luna 2 was the first man-made object to impact the lunar surface, and Luna 3 provided the first photographs of the Moon's far side.

q: What was the significance of the Mariner missions?
Which probes were used to study Mars and Venus during the Space Race?
What did the Mariner program achieve?
a: The Mariner program consisted of a series of robotic probes launched by NASA to explore the inner solar system. These missions provided the first close-up images of Mars and Venus, expanding scientific knowledge beyond the Earth-Moon system.

q: What was the Voskhod program?
Which Soviet program featured the first multi-person crew in space?
What was the outcome of the Voskhod missions?
a: Voskhod was a short-lived Soviet program that served as a transition between Vostok and Soyuz. It is most notable for Voskhod 2, where Alexei Leonov performed the first-ever spacewalk in March 1965.
